{{Use dmy dates|date=December 2019}}
{{Primary sources|date=December 2019}}
'''Georges Vendryès''' or '''Georges Vendryes''' (1920 – 16 September 2014) was a French physicist who played a significant role in the French nuclear industry and is considered the "father" of [[fast breeder reactor]] technology, for which he received the [[Enrico Fermi Prize]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://science.osti.gov/fermi/Award-Laureates/1980s/vendryes |publisher=US DOE office of science|title=FERMI George Vendryes, 1984 &#124; U.S. DOE Office of Science (SC)|date=28 December 2010 }}</ref> and [[Japan Prize]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.japanprize.jp/en/prize_past_1988_prize01.html |publisher=Japan Prize|title=The Japan Prize Foundation}}</ref>

Vendryes studied at the [[École Polytechnique]] and the [[École des Ponts et Chaussées]] and received his doctorate in nuclear physics at the [[Sorbonne University|Sorbonne]]. From 1948 he was employed by the French nuclear research authority [[French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission|CEA]], where he made his first experiments under [[Frédéric Joliot-Curie]]. At the CEA he worked on neutron transport experiments and research and development of different type of reactors including controlled thermonuclear fusion. and was significant in the construction of various important installations such as Harmonie (1965), Masurca (1966), [[Rapsodie]] (1967), Phenix (1973) and [[Superphénix]] (1985).<ref>{{cite book |url=https://inis.iaea.org/search/searchsinglerecord.aspx?recordsFor=SingleRecord&RN=50033178 |publisher=International Nuclear Information System|title=INIS Repository Search - Single Result|series=Georges Vendryes, le 'pere' des reacteurs a neutrons rapides |year=2019 }}</ref>

He was appointed Director of the Nuclear Reactors Department of the CEA in 1971, and was Adviser to the CEA Administrator General from 1983 to 1988.

In 1984 he received the Enrico Fermi Prize and in 1988 he received the Japan Prize. He was an officer of the [[Legion of Honour|Legion of Honor]] and Grand Officer of the [[Ordre national du Mérite]] and was awarded the Federal Cross of Merit. He was a member of the National Academy of Engineering and Honorary Vice President of the CEA. In 2007, he received the first Eminent Scientist Award from the Indian Nuclear Society.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://in.ambafrance.org/Dr-Georges-VENDRYES-Honorary-Vice |publisher=French embassy in India|title=Dr Georges VENDRYES, Honorary Vice-President, French Atomic Energy Commission, received the "INS Eminent Scientist Award 2007"}}</ref>

Georges Vendryes died on 16 September 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sfen.org/rgn/deces-georges-vendryes-pere-reacteurs-nucleaires-neutrons-rapides |title=Décès de Georges Vendryes, Père des réacteurs nucléaires à neutrons rapides |trans-title=Death of Georges Vendryes, Father of Fast Neutron Nuclear Reactors |publisher=Société française d'énergie nucléaire |language=French |date=2014-09-23 |access-date=2019-12-25}}</ref>
